On the day Wùyín,
Shǐxīng Wáng Dàn, Píngxī Jiāngjūn (General Who Quells the West) and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was promoted in title to Ānxī Jiāngjūn (General Who Pacifies the West).
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Xiàhóu Xiáng, Grand Master of the Right of the Glorious Palace, was appointed Assistant Director of the Left of the Department of State Affairs.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Xiàhóu Xiáng, Assistant Director of the Left of the Department of State Affairs, died.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Cháng Yōnghé, Army Commander of the Wèi Huáiyáng Garrison, submitted with the city.
Huòzhōu was established by dividing Yùzhōu.
In the seventh year, spring, the first month, on the day Yǐyǒu (the new moon),
an imperial edict stated:
"Establishing the state and ruling the people,
establishing education is the foremost priority.
If learning is neglected,
excellent growth has no foundation.
We, having initiated Our brilliant mandate
and brightly inhabited the realm,
though We have diligently pursued elegant pursuits
and concurrently expounded upon arts and letters,
the completion of talent has not been widespread,
and the foundation of purpose is still lacking.
This is not the means by which to mold noble offspring
and bring them into proper standards.
We desire to ceremoniously emphasize deference and seniority,
setting the standard from the household to the state.
Now, where Our reputation and instruction extend,
barbarians and Chinese share the same customs.
It is fitting to greatly establish schools
and broadly invite the sons of officials,
pursuing the Ten Relationships
and promoting the Three Virtues,
so that the influence of molding and cultivation reaches far,
and subtle words are once again manifested."
Wáng Mào, *Zhōngwèi Jiāngjūn* (Central Guard General) and concurrently Chief Steward of the Crown Prince, was promoted in title to Chēqí Jiāngjūn (General of Chariots and Cavalry).
On the day Wùxū,
the Shénlóng (Divine Dragon) and Rénhǔ (Benevolent Tiger) watchtowers were built outside the Duānmén and Dàsīmǎ Mén (Gates of the Grand Marshal).
On the day Rénzǐ,
Cáo Jǐngzōng, General Regulating the Army, was appointed *Zhōngwèi Jiāngjūn*.
Xiāo Jǐng, Commandant of the Guards, concurrently held the title of *Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn*.
In the second month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Lújiāng Qián Xiàn acquired two bronze bells.
New national gates were constructed south of Yuèchéng.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the number of troops under the Zhènwèi Jūn (Garrison Guard Army) and below was increased by varying degrees.
On the day Gēngwǔ,

an edict ordered that in every *zhōu* (province), *jùn* (commandery), and *xiàn* (county), one *zhōuwàng* (Provincial Hope), one *jùnzōng* (Commandery Patriarch), and one *xiāngháo* (Local Magnate) be established,
specializing in searching out and recommending talent.
On the day Yǐhài,
Gāolì Wáng Gāo Yún, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, was appointed Fǔdōng Dàjiāngjūn (Grand General Who Stabilizes the East)
and *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*.
Lǚ Sēngzhēn, Píngběi Jiāngjūn and Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, was appointed *Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn*.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Chángshā Wáng Shēnyè, Central Protector of the Army, was appointed Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu.
Xiāo Jǐng, concurrently *Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn*, was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
Liǔ Qìngyuǎn, Inspector of Yōngzhōu, was appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn (Protector of the Army General).
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
the Crown Prince married his consort.
An amnesty was granted for capital offenses and lesser crimes.
Presents were distributed to court officials and palace attendants, varying by rank.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Mó líng Xiàn acquired one spirit turtle.
On the day Wùyín,
Yúyáo Xiàn acquired two ancient bronze swords.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐhài,
an edict restored the Sūngzhèng (Court of the Imperial Clan), Tàipú (Court of the Imperial Stud), Dàjiàng (Court of the Imperial Treasury), and Hónglú (Court of the Imperial Regalia).
Furthermore, Tàifǔ (Court of the Imperial Storehouses) and Tàizhōu (Court of Imperial Vessels) were added,
making a total of twelve ministers, as previously established.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Ānchéng Wáng Xiù, Píngnán Jiāngjūn and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, was appointed Píngxī Jiāngjūn (General Who Quells the West) and Inspector of Jīngzhōu.
Shǐxīng Wáng Dàn, Ānxī Jiāngjūn and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
Cáo Jǐngzōng, *Zhōngwèi Jiāngjūn*, was appointed Ānnán Jiāngjūn (General Who Pacifies the South) and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the residents within a circumference of five *lǐ* around the Jiànlíng and Xiūlíng tombs were resettled.
The tomb superintendents (*língjiān*) were renamed directors (*línglìng*).
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Dīnghài,
the moon eclipsed Dī (Lunar Mansion).
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Cáo Jǐngzōng, Ānnán Jiāngjūn and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, died.
On the day Dīngsì,
an amnesty was granted for those accused of capital offenses and lesser crimes whose cases had not yet been formally closed.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Ānchéng Wáng Xiù, Píngxī Jiāngjūn and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was promoted in title to Ānxī Jiāngjūn.
Póyáng Wáng Huī, Yúnhuī Jiāngjūn (General of Cloud Banners) and Inspector of Yǐngzhōu, was promoted in title to Píngxī Jiāngjūn.
The Lǎorén Xīng (Canopus) was visible.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīnghài,
an edict stated:
“To travel for grazing and pasturage is certainly necessary,
as established by Jī Wén's precedent;
to impose penalties for pheasants and rabbits [hunted in season]
caused Jiāng Xuān to suffer demotion.
Marshes, swamps, mountains, and forests
are where materials for construction are produced,
and the use of the axe
is relied upon by every household.
However, successive generations recently
have all added restrictions and prohibitions,
how can this be described as sharing profit with the people
and bestowing grace upon the multitude?
Therefore, all fields and military colonies belonging to the government which are currently subject to prohibition and cultivation
may all have their customary restrictions removed.”
On the day Rénchén,
the office of Tóngzǐ Fèngchē Láng (Attendant Official of the Carriage, held by a youth) was established.
On the day Guǐsì,
imperial son Jì was established as the King of Nánkāng Commandery.
On the day Jǐhài,
the moon encroached upon the constellation Dōngjǐng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Zhāng Jì, the Administrator of Wúxīng, was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè (Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs).
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Xǔ Jìngzhēn, the garrison commander of Wèi's Yángguān, defected with his city.
An edict commanded a massive northern expedition.
Hùjūn Jiāngjūn (General Protecting the Army) Xiàoxīng Wáng Dàn was appointed Píngběi Jiāngjūn (General Pacifying the North),
leading the troops to advance into Qīng [Province];
Chējì Jiāngjūn (General of Chariots and Cavalry) Wáng Mào led troops toward Sùyù.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Bái Zàoshēng, the garrison commander of Wèi's Xuánhù,
and Hú Xùn, the Inspector of Yùzhōu, submitted with their cities.
Zàoshēng was appointed Zhènběi Jiāngjūn (General Guarding the North) and Inspector of Sīzhōu,
and Xùn was appointed Píngběi Jiāngjūn and Inspector of Yùzhōu.
The eleventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
Yín County reported the descent of sweet dew (gānlù).
The eighth year, spring, the first month, on the day Xīnsì,
the Imperial Carriage personally offered sacrifice in the Southern Suburbs,
granted a general amnesty,
and bestowed a year of salary and allowances upon all civil and military officials, internal and external.
On the day Rénchén,
Chéng Jǐngjùn, Wèi's Zhengdōng Cānjūn (Staff Officer to the General Who Punishes the East), beheaded Yán Zhòngbǎo, the commander of Sùyù city,
and submitted with the city.
The second month, on the day Rénxū,
the Star of the Elderly (Lǎorén Xīng, Canopus) appeared.
Summer, the fourth month,
Nánliángzhōu was established from the former North Bāxī Commandery.
On the day Wùshēn,
Hùjūn Jiāngjūn Xiàoxīng Wáng Dàn was appointed Zhōngwèi Jiāngjūn (General of the Central Guard),
Sītú (Minister of Works) and Acting Tàizǐ Tàifù (Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent) Línchuān Wáng Hóng was appointed Sīkōng (Minister of Works) and Inspector of Yángzhōu,

and Chējì Jiāngjūn and concurrently Lǐng Tàizǐ Zhànshì (Head of the Household Establishment of the Heir Apparent) Wáng Mào was granted the title Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī (Establishing a Manor and Enjoying the Same Privileges as the Three Excellencies) while retaining his original rank.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Lǐ Guóxīng, the commander of Wèi's Chǔwáng City, defected with his city.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn (General of the Central Army) and Dānyáng Yǐn (Magistrate of Dānyáng) Wáng Yíng was appointed Yòu Guānglù Dàfū (Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).
The fifth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
an edict stated:
“Studying in order to engage in governance
was earnestly pursued by the ancient sages;
salary being inherent therein
is also an established former matter.
I intend to illuminate the principles of governance
and always emphasize Confucian scholarship.
Stopping one's carriage at the entrance and opening schools
is what I am constantly attending to.
Therefore, carrying satchels [of books] has become customary,
and those of the highest academic rank emerge occasionally.
They should be placed in important official posts
and decorated with azure and purple [robes of office].
Any person who can thoroughly understand a single classic and remains diligent from beginning to end,
after their abilities are measured and verified,
may be selected and appointed to office according to their capacity.
Even if they are mere cattle supervisors or sheep sellers,
from humble families or later-ranking clans,
they should all be tested for official service according to their talent,
without being neglected or excluded.”
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Guǐsì,
Bālíng Wáng Xiāo Bǎoyì died.
The eighth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
the Star of the Elderly appeared.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn Xiàoxīng Wáng Dàn was appointed Zhènběi Jiāngjūn and Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu,
and Chángshā Wáng Shēnyè, the Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, was appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
The ninth year, spring, the first month, on the day Yǐhài,

Shàngshū Lìng (Director of the Department of State Affairs) and Acting Tàizǐ Shàofù (Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent) Shěn Yuē was appointed Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū (Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness),
retaining his status as Acting Shàofù;
Yòu Guānglù Dàfū Wáng Yíng was appointed Shàngshū Lìng;
Acting Zhōngfǔ Jiāngjūn (General Who Soothes the Center) Jiàn'ān Wáng Wěi was concurrently appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn;
Zhènběi Jiāngjūn and Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu Xiàoxīng Wáng Dàn was appointed Zhènxī Jiāngjūn (General Who Guards the West) and Inspector of Yìzhōu;
and Tàicháng Qīng (Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices) Wáng Liàng was appointed Zhōngshū Jiān (Director of the Central Secretariat).
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Qīngchē Jiāngjūn (General of Light Chariots) Jìn'ān Wáng Gāng was appointed Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu.
On the day Gēngyín,
a new embankment along the Huái River was constructed.
The northern bank extended from Shítóu to Dōngyě,
and the southern bank extended from Hòuzhǔ Límén to Sānqiáo.
The third month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the Imperial Carriage proceeded to the Guózǐ Xué (Imperial Academy),
personally attended the lectures,
and bestowed silk upon the Guózǐ Jìjiǔ (Libationer of the Imperial Academy) and others, each receiving different amounts.
On the day Yǐwèi,
an edict stated:
“Princes studying
was recorded in the Lǐ Jīng (Classic of Rites),
and prominent families all participating
was indeed a former proclamation,
the means by which principles and morality are broadly expanded
and the way of teaching is greatly extended.
Now that the Chéngjūn (Grand Harmony, referring to the Imperial Academy) is greatly opened,
the noble sons defer to their elders in age [in study],
and starting from them downwards,
all should practice their studies.
The sons of the Heir Apparent, Kings, and Marquises,
who are of an age to follow a teacher,
are ordered to enroll in the Academy.”
The state of Yútián sent envoys to present local products.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Dīngsì,
the selection criteria for the Wǔdū Lìshǐ (Clerks of the Five Bureaus) of the Department of State Affairs were revised to use those from humble streams [of society].
The state of Línyì sent an envoy to present one white monkey.
The fifth month, on the day Jǐhài,
an edict stated:
“I seek to hear opinions and attend to governance,
never forgetting the passage of time until sunset,
but the various matters of the hundred offices
do not follow a single path.
Applying them according to the situation
is appropriate in each case.
If the words of the multitude are not collectively gathered,
I will have no means to prepare for this personal observation.
From now on, in the Tái Gé (Court Chambers), Shěng Fǔ (Secretariats), Zhōu Jùn (Provinces and Commanderies), and Zhèn Shù (Garrison Posts), wherever there are official functionaries,
they should convene discussions regularly,
each presenting suggestions for improvement or detriment,
and fully report them.”
Zhōngshū Jiān Wáng Liàng died.
The sixth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
thieves murdered Zhū Sēngyǒng, the Administrator of Xuānchéng.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Zhōngfǔ Jiāngjūn and concurrently Lǐng Hùjūn Jiàn'ān Wáng Wěi was appointed Zhènnán Jiāngjūn (General Who Guards the South) and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu.
The intercalary month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the thieves from Xuānchéng moved on to raid Wúxīng County.
Cài Zǔn, the Administrator, led a campaign and pacified them.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jǐsì,
the Star of the Elderly appeared.
Winter, the twelfth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the Imperial Carriage proceeded to the Guózǐ Xué,
tested the students of noble families (zhòuzǐ),
and bestowed gifts upon the officials responsible for instruction and supervision, each receiving different amounts.
The tenth year, spring, the first month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the Imperial Carriage personally offered sacrifice in the Southern Suburbs,
granted a great amnesty to the world,
and bestowed two years of salary and allowances upon those residing in office and handling affairs.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè Zhāng Jì was appointed Ānběi Jiāngjūn (General Who Pacifies the North) and Inspector of Qīng and Jì Two Provinces,
and Póyáng Wáng Huī, the Inspector of Yǐngzhōu, was appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Yùzhāng Wáng Zōng, the Inspector of Nánxúzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Yǐngzhōu,
and Qīngchē Jiāngjūn Nánkāng Wáng Jì was appointed Inspector of Nánxúzhōu.
On the day Wùshēn,
one Zōuyú (an auspicious beast)
was seen in Huáróng County, Jīngzhōu.
Zuǒ Mín Shàngshū (Director of the Left Bureau of the People) Wáng Jiǎn was appointed Lìbù Shàngshū (Director of the Ministry of Personnel).
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Imperial Carriage personally offered sacrifice in the Míngtáng (Bright Hall).
The third month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
thieves murdered Dèng Zhé, the Administrator of Dōngguǎn and Lángyé Two Commanderies,
and used Qúshān to draw in the Wèi army.
Zhènyuǎn Jiāngjūn (General Who Manifests Distance) Mǎ Xiānpǐn was dispatched to suppress them.
In this month,
Lú Chǎng, Wèi's Inspector of Xúzhōu, led troops to advance towards Qúshān.
Summer, the fifth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
a one-horned black turtle was captured in Ānfēng County.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Lǐngjūn (Commander of the Palace Guard) Lü Sēngzhēn died.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Guózǐ Jìjiǔ Zhāng Chōng was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè,
and Tàizǐ Zhànshì Liǔ Qìngyuǎn was appointed Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn.
The sixth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
a stem of auspicious lotus with three blossoms grew in the Lèyóu Yuàn park.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *bǐng chén*,
an edict stated:
“In the past, the Dukes and Ministers presented matters face-to-face,
recorded in previous histories;
the Prefects and Vice-Ministers submitted memorials on the steps of the palace,
clearly documented across generations.
This was how they governed the myriad achievements [of the state]
and completed the various affairs.
When the Jìn (Jìn) dynasty declined,
baseless extravagance became the custom.
Since then, as this practice has been inherited,
the failures have become increasingly serious.
Consequently, the military tents labor in vain,
lacking the memorials of Duke Jí (Jí Gōng);
the vermilion courtyard is opened needlessly,
missing the footprints of Master Zhèng (Zhèng Shēng).
The officials of the Three *Huái* and Eight Seats [high-ranking ministers],
and the hundred officials who have duties,
should offer their discussions.
They may enter and present their petitions,
hoping to utilize comprehensive counsel,
and slightly correct My deficiencies.”
Ninth month, on the day *bǐng shēn*,
there was a rumbling sound from the northwest in the sky,
and a red vapor descended to the earth.
Winter, twelfth month, on the day *guǐ yǒu*,
a mountain carriage was seen in Línchéng (Línchéng) County.
On the day *gēng chén*,
Mǎ Xiānpǐn (Mǎ Xiānpǐn) heavily defeated the Wèi (Wèi) army,
beheading and taking captive over 100,000 men,
and recaptured Qúshān (Qúshān) City.
This year,
the triple-story towers on the palace city gates were constructed for the first time, and two new avenues were opened.
The State of Dàngchāng (Dàngchāng) sent envoys to present local products.
Eleventh year, spring, first month, on the day *rén chén*,
an edict stated:
“The penal code sympathizes with the elderly,
and crimes do not extend to wives and children.
The rites clearly document this,
and history confirms these past events.
This is how compassion and sympathy are demonstrated,
ensuring that punishment does not reach certain individuals.
However, in recent times, inheriting previous practices,
the legal net has become increasingly strict,
so that young children and those with white hair [the elderly]
are equally implicated in guilt.
Although deterring evil and encouraging goodness
requires exhausting all regulatory measures,
the displacement of the old and young
is truly lamentable.
Henceforth, in households of criminals undergoing banishment or those whose crimes warrant compulsory labor,
if there are elderly or young people,
their transport shall be halted.”
Shěn Yuē (Shěn Yuē), who held the posts of Grand Master of the Left Glorious Happiness and acting Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, was promoted to Special Advancement (*Tèjìn*).
Wěi (Wěi), Prince of Jiàn’ān (Jiàn’ān), General Who Guards the South and Governor of Jiāngzhōu (Jiāngzhōu), was granted the ceremony of the Three Ducal Ministers.
Hóng (Hóng), Prince of Línchuān (Línchuān), Minister of Works (*Sīkōng*) and Governor of Yángzhōu (Yángzhōu), was promoted to Grand Commandant (*Tàiwèi*).
Wáng Mào (Wáng Mào), General of Agile Cavalry, was made Minister of Works (*Sīkōng*).
Wáng Yíng (Wáng Yíng), Prefect of the Masters of Writing and General of the Cloud Banner, was promoted to the title of General Who Pacifies the Left.
Zhāng Jì (Zhāng Jì), General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of the two provinces of Qīng (Qīng) and Jì (Jì), was promoted to the title of General Who Guards the North.
Second month, on the day *wù chén*,
wild silkworms formed cocoons in the two commanderies of Xīnchāng (Xīnchāng) and Jìyáng (Jìyáng).
Third month, on the day *dīng sì*,
a partial amnesty was granted in the two provinces of Yáng (Yáng) and Xú (Xú).
The Xījìng (Xījìng) Altar was constructed on Zhōng Shān (Zhōng Shān).
On the day *gēng shēn*,
the State of Gāolì (Gāolì) sent envoys to present local products.
Fourth month, on the day *wù zǐ*,
an edict stated:
“Last year at Qúshān (Qúshān), a great annihilation of the enemy was achieved.
It would be appropriate to build a monumental mound of captured heads (*jīng guān*)
to signal the military achievements;
however, attacking the guilty and comforting the populace
is the glorious tradition of the august kings,
and covering the exposed skeletons and burying the corpses
is the concern of the benevolent.
Therefore, instruct Qīngzhōu (Qīngzhōu) to collect and bury all remains.”

Yuán Áng (Yuán Áng), the concurrent Vice Director of the Right of the Masters of Writing, was formally appointed Vice Director of the Right of the Masters of Writing.
On the day *bǐng yín*,
an edict stated:
“Covering exposed skeletons and burying corpses
is an important tenet of the Zhōu (Zhōu) classics,
and providing coffins and boxes
is a beautiful matter recorded in Hàn (Hàn) policy.
We have pondered this matter in silence,
and have frequently exerted ourselves in this regard.
Orders for the collection and burial of remains
have been urgently issued out of compassion;
yet, in distant and deep-lying districts,
compliance with the order has not been thorough.
White bones lie scattered along the roadsides,
appearing frequently.
While We speak of pitying the sunken and decaying,
Our compassion is increasingly strained.
It is hereby clearly commanded to regions near and far
to patrol their respective boundaries.
If abandoned remains are found unburied,
or if simple grass shrouds have not been replaced,
they should immediately be collected and interred,
and coffins and burial equipment should be supplied according to need.
Thus, the souls who weep at night may find solace,
and the bones exposed to frost may find rest.”

In the first month of spring in the fourteenth year, on the day *yǐsì* (the new moon),
the crown prince was capped.
A general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
Those who succeeded their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
Princes and dukes downward were bestowed gifts, each according to their station.
Homage and congratulatory rituals from near and far were suspended.
On *bǐngwǔ*,
Ān Zuǒ Jiāngjūn and Shàngshū Lìng Wáng Yíng was promoted to Zhōng Quán Jiāngjūn.
Zhèn Xī Jiāngjūn Shǐxīng Wáng Dàn was appointed Zhōng Fǔ Jiāngjūn.
On *xīnhài*,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the southern suburb.
An imperial edict stated:
"I reverently attend to the bright sacrifices,
and solemnly serve the supreme spirits.
I enter the bamboo palace and ascend the Grand Altar,
donning the fur robe and ceremonial cap to present the dark jade disc.
As the offerings of firewood and distant gaze have ascended,
sincerity and reverence have been fully expressed.
I ponder how to respond to the celestial origin [Qiányuán],
and broadly propagate moral instruction.
Yet, there are deficiencies in the path of governance,
and many aspects of law and administration remain obscure.
I truly await the assembly of talents
to bring peace to the myriad accomplishments.
Therefore, this is to be proclaimed far and wide,
to broadly gather exceptional individuals.
If there are those who are truly outstanding in their communities,
exemplary in their localities,
living in reclusion in their hills and gardens,
not seeking fame or advancement,
concealing their abilities and awaiting their time,
and have not yet been selected;
or those who are贤良 (xiánliáng - virtuous and good), 方正 (fāngzhèng - upright),
孝悌 (xiàotì - filial and fraternal), or 力田 (lìtián - diligent in agriculture),
they should all be immediately reported
with their names submitted in full.
They shall be elevated to public service [Zhōuháng],
and tested in the administration of various districts and cities,
so that all officials may diligently perform their duties,
and the myriad people have no hidden grievances.
Furthermore, as the severity of punishments varies with the times and laws are adjusted accordingly,
previously, punishments such as tattooing and nose-cutting
were used to replace capital punishment.
Yet, if one wishes to repent and reform,
the path is blocked.
All these may be abolished."
On *bǐngyín*,

In the ninth month, on *guǐhài*,
Chángshā Wáng Shēnyè was appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
The Lángyáxiū State sent envoys to present local products.
In the first month of spring in the fifteenth year, on *jǐsì*,
an imperial edict stated:
"Observing the times and establishing teachings is what the king's governance prioritizes.
To benefit all equally
is truly to uphold the fundamental,
and changing customs to achieve good governance
all stems from this.
Recently, orders for reform
have been issued as needed,
but the essence of relaxation and strictness
has not reached its proper balance.
The people's sufferings are still numerous,
and uprightness and fairness are still scarce.
This is why I gaze upon the dangling pearls [on my crown] with heavy heart,
and sigh when meeting with jade and silk.
Let this be proclaimed throughout the four directions:
if there are government policies inconvenient to the people,
the relevant authorities shall list them and report them.
If local officials are commendably clean,
or if they are corrupt and harmful,
they should be separately reported,
and promotions or demotions will be carried out.
Senior officials should encourage and supervise,
and personally inspect dikes and embankments,
ensuring none are left unrepaired,
to avoid hindering agricultural affairs.
Taxes at passes and markets
may sometimes be unfair;
local authorities should review them in due course
and generously reduce the old rates."
In the third month, on the day *wùchén* (the new moon),

In the tenth month of winter, on *wùwǔ*,

In the eleventh month, on *dīngmǎo*,

On *rénwǔ*,
Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Wéi Ruì was appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
In the first month of spring in the sixteenth year, on *xīnwèi*,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the southern suburb.
An imperial edict stated:
"I sit on the throne contemplating governance,
but the path of administration remains unclear.
Toiling from dawn,
many years have passed.
Now, as Tàihào governs the vital energy,
and Gōumáng initiates the season,
ascending to the center and moving towards the yang,
reverent sacrifices have been fully expressed.
It is essential to receive Heaven's blessings,
and spread this harmonious benevolence.
For the extremely poor households,
this year's three taxes shall not be collected.
For those without land or occupation,
provisions shall be assessed and granted according to local circumstances.
If people give birth to children,
they shall be given generous exemptions according to regulations.
Orphans, the elderly, and widows who cannot support themselves
shall all receive additional relief.
Proclaim this throughout the four directions.
All prefectures, commanderies, and counties
shall promptly handle lawsuits,
ensuring no grievances are left unaddressed,
as if personally overseen."
In the second month, on *gēngxū*,

In the third month, on *bǐngzǐ*,

In the sixth month, on *wùshēn*,

In the seventh month, on *dīngchǒu*,

In the spring, the first month, on the *dìngsì* day, the first day of the seventeenth year of Tiānjiān,
an imperial edict stated:
"The origin of joy
is the constant nature of all sentient beings;
to enrich the people and stabilize their homes
is the universal rule for governing the world.
I pity these common people,
never forgetting their plight at dawn,
and have frequently implemented strategies for increasing population and prosperity,
and often extended grace and compassion.
However, the number of registered households has not grown,
and migration still occurs.
Lightly leaving one's hometown,
how could that be their original intention?
Their assets and livelihoods are likely deficient,
and they have no means to return on their own;
the desire to return to their nest
cannot be appeased.
Now, as the New Year begins,
all things are renewed.
I wish to enable the black-haired people
to each settle in their former places.
This will ensure that no county has fallow land,
and no city has idle people.
The sounds of chickens and dogs will be heard between homes,
and mulberry and ramie fields will crisscross paths.
All people in the empire
who have migrated to other territories,
before the first day of the first month of the seventeenth year of Tiānjiān,
may be granted half a year of grace
to all return to their original homes,
and be exempted from taxes for three years.
For those who have wandered too far,
the travel time will be appropriately extended.
If there are those who are unwilling to return,
they should be registered as commoners in their current locality
and pay taxes according to the old rates.
If, after their migration,
there are no longer residences available in their original hometown,
the village officials, the three elders (*sānlǎo*), and other relatives
shall immediately go to the county
to apply for official land and official residences within the village,
to allow them to be accommodated,
so that those who yearn for their roots have a place to return to.

Regarding all those who, due to their involvement in market tolls and other offices, were found to have committed embezzlement, theft, or fraudulent reductions, and were consequently subject to confiscation of property,
their fields, residences, carts, and oxen
are the means of people's livelihood,
and should not all be confiscated.
A generous portion should be allocated and retained for them,
to enable them to sustain themselves.
Wealthy merchants and households
are also prohibited from abruptly acquiring and merging properties.
For those who have fled or rebelled,
regardless of the severity of their crime,
all are permitted to surrender
and return to the ranks of commoners.
If there are any who were detained,
they shall return to their original service.
These regulations shall be compiled
and made known to all."
In the second month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Zhènbei Jiāngjūn and Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Ānchéng Wáng Xiù passed away.
On the *jiǎchén* day,

On the *bǐngshēn* day,

In the summer, the fifth month, on the *wùyín* day,

On the *jǐmǎo* day, the kingdom of Gānlìguó sent envoys to offer local products.
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn Xiāo Jǐng was appointed Ānyòu Jiāngjūn,
Supervising Yángzhōu.

On the *guǐmǎo* day,

An imperial edict stated that for military personnel, servants, and slaves,

and females aged fifty and above,
should be exempted and become commoners.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn and Acting Sītú Línchuān Wáng Hóng was appointed Zhōngshū Jiān and Sītú.
In the eleventh month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Nánpíng Wáng Wěi was appointed Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
In the spring, the first month, on the *jiǎshēn* day of the eighteenth year of Tiānjiān,
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn Póyáng Wáng Huī was appointed Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ.
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Shǐxīng Wáng Dàn was appointed Zhōngfǔ Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Lǐngjūn.
Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè Yuán Áng was appointed Shàngshū Lìng.
Shàngshū Yòu Púyè Wáng Jiàn was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè.
Tàizǐ Zhānshì Xú Miǎn was appointed Shàngshū Yòu Púyè.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Southern Suburb.
Those who practiced filial piety, fraternal duty, and diligently worked the fields were granted one noble rank.
In the second month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
the Old Man Star was sighted.
In the fourth month, on the *dìngsì* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Old Man Star was sighted.
The kingdoms of Yútián and Fúnán each sent envoys to offer local products.

On the *xīnsì* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Southern Suburb.
An imperial edict stated:
"The Spring deity commands the *qì*,
and with reverence and solemnity, sacrifices are offered.
With sincere devotion, the earthenware and gourds are presented,
and the blue jade is prepared with proper ritual.
I wish to follow the covering of heaven
and spread this nurturing care.
All commoners who are elderly and solitary, or orphaned and young, and cannot sustain themselves,
the responsible prefectures and counties shall all take them in and care for them,
providing them with clothing and food,
always ensuring they are adequately provided,
until the end of their lives.
Furthermore, an 'Orphans and Solitary Garden' shall be established in the capital,
so that orphaned youth have a home,
and those with white hair do not suffer want.
If their lives end,
they shall be given a generous burial.
For especially poor households,
rent and taxes shall not be collected."
On the *wùzǐ* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
In the second month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Míngtáng.
In the third month, on the *gēngyín* day,
there was heavy snow,
three *chǐ* deep on level ground.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
the Northern and Southern Suburbs were rebuilt.
On the day Bǐngchén,
an edict stated:
“To reverently comply with Hào Tiān (Vast Heaven),
observing celestial phenomena without error,
personally wielding the plow,
and dedicating utmost reverence,
thereby harmonizing with the constellation Xīngniǎo (Star Bird) above,
and instructing the people in seasonal tasks below,
managing the spring plowing in order,
the principle does not lie in the south.
Former dynasties followed this tradition,
but it deviates from the rites and regulations.
It is permissible to seek a fertile plain
in the Zhèn direction (east),
and establish one thousand mù there,
to truly conform to the old regulations.”
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Wǎnyǎn Diàn (Jade Hall) caught fire,
and the fire spread to three thousand rooms in the inner palace.
On the day Dīngsì,
an edict stated:
“Princes, dukes, ministers, and officials
are now submitting memorials to congratulate on auspicious omens.
Although this expresses the sincerity of all officials for the state,
I feel much shame in my heart.
If my beneficence truly flowed like rivers and springs,
and compassion reached all living things,
the climate were temperate like jade candles,
and governance achieved great peace,
then auspicious signs would descend,
and there would be no shame in my virtue.
However, the path of governance has many shortcomings,
and pure transformation has not yet solidified.
How can this harmonize with the celestial order above,
and receive profound blessings from afar?
This merely further reveals my inadequacy,
and adds to its faults.
From now on, the congratulations on auspicious omens should cease.”
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Wén Sēngmíng, General of Inspiring Awe and Inspector of Yìzhōu, revolted with his prefecture and defected to Wèi.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Péi Suì, acting Grand Architect, was granted a staff of authority,
and led all armies to launch a northern expedition.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Elder Star (Canopus) was sighted.
Huán Shūxīng, Wèi Inspector of Jīngzhōu, led his troops and surrendered.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīnghài,
in Shǐpíng Prefecture, Shígǔ Cūn (Stone Drum Village) spontaneously opened up into a well,
six chǐ and six cùn square,
and thirty-two zhàng deep.
In the winter, eleventh month,
the states of Bǎijì and Xīnluó each sent envoys to present local products.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùchén,
Yú Lóng, King of Bǎijì and General Who Quells the East, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East.
In the third year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Yuán Áng, Director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Supervisor of the Central Secretariat;
Wáng Jiǎn, Administrator of Wújùn, was appointed Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs;
Wáng Fèn, Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
On the day Gēngxū,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Xiāo Xù, Prince of Lúlíng and General Who Manifests Awe, was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
In the third month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Xiāo Píng, Prince of Bālíng, passed away.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Liú Duān, Prince of Rǔyīn, passed away.
In the fifth month, on the first day Rénchén,
there was a solar eclipse,
which was total.
On the day Guǐsì,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and announced to the four directions.
The grievances and hardships of the people
were to be reported immediately.
Princes, dukes, and all officials were to submit sealed memorials,
and regional governors and prefectures were to recommend worthy, upright, and outspoken individuals.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the construction of the two suburbs and the Xíjiàn (Ceremonial Field) was completed,
and artisans were rewarded with varying gifts.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Elder Star was sighted.
The states of Pólì and Báití each sent envoys to present local products.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Yuán Áng, Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, was promoted to General of the Central Guard.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Xiāo Dàn, Prince of Shǐxīng, General of the Guard, Kàifǔ Yítóng Sānsī (Establishing a Mansion with the Same Privileges as the Three Dukes), and General of the Palace Guard, passed away.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Xiāo Yuānzǎo, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, was appointed General of the Palace Guard.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburb,
and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
All who were destitute and ill
were to be relieved and comforted,
and this was announced to the four directions.
At that time, judicial cases were also handled.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Míngtáng (Bright Hall).
In the second month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the Elder Star was sighted.
On the day Yǐhài,
the emperor personally plowed the Xíjiàn.
An edict stated:
“The meaning of plowing the Xíjiàn is indeed great!
It is from this that sacrificial grains arise,
and ritual ceremonies are established.
Ancient sagely kings all practiced this.
Mindful of the eight policies,
I establish these thousand mù,
and princes, dukes, and all officials
are respectfully diligent in its rituals,
completing the nine plowings,
and the fragrant offerings never cease.
Moreover, the winds and clouds harmonize with the seasons,
and the weather is splendid and glorious.
Observing this auspicious occasion,
I desire to add encouragement.
This is to be announced far and wide,
to widely open up good fields,
so that public and private farmlands
fully utilize the land's bounty.
If those who wish to engage in agriculture lack grain seeds,
they shall also be granted loans and relief,
always ensuring ample provision.
Filial and fraternal individuals who diligently farm shall be granted one rank of nobility.
The officials overseeing the ceremonial plowing
shall be rewarded with wine on a set day.”
In the third month, on the day Rénmín,
Xiāo Zōng, Prince of Yùzhāng and General Who Guards the Right, was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Yǎnzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Xìnzhōu was established by dividing Yìzhōu;
Àizhōu was established by dividing Jiāozhōu;
Chéngzhōu, Nándìngzhōu, Hézhōu, and Jiànzhōu were established by dividing Guǎngzhōu;
Yìzhōu was established by dividing Huòzhōu.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
the Elder Star was sighted.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Yuán Áng, Supervisor of the Central Secretariat and General of the Central Guard, was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs,
retaining his original title and the Kàifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Chāng Yìzhī, General of the Guard, passed away.
In the eleventh month, on the first day Guǐwèi,
there was a solar eclipse.
Tàibái (Venus) was visible during the day.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Wáng Jiǎn, Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
iron coins were first cast.
The state of Lángyáxiū sent envoys to present local products.
In the fifth year, spring, first month,
Xiāo Wěi, Prince of Nánpíng, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left, and Kàifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, was appointed Grand General Who Guards the Guard,
and re-appointed Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness,
with the Yítóng Sānsī as before.
Póyáng Wáng Huī, Prince of Póyáng, General Who Conquers the West, Kàifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
Xiàhóu Dǎn, Grand Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, was appointed Central Protector of the Army.
Wáng Fèn, Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness, was appointed Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness,
and additionally granted Special Advance.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Xiāo Zōng, Prince of Yùzhāng, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Southern Yǎnzhōu, was promoted to General Who Guards the North.
Jìn'ān Wáng Gāng, Prince of Jìn'ān, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yōngzhōu, was promoted to General Who Anshies the North.
In the second month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Wáng Fèn, Special Advance and Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness, passed away.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Elder Star was sighted.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Eastern Yángzhōu was established by dividing Yángzhōu and Jiāngzhōu.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Xiāo Jī, Prince of Nánkāng and General of Cloud Banners, was appointed Inspector of Jiāngzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
dragons fought at Qǔ'ā Wáng Pō (King's Slope in Qǔ'ā),
and then traveled west to Jiànlíng Chéng (Jiànlíng City).
Along their path, trees were toppled and broken,
and the ground was opened up for tens of zhàng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Wǔlíng Wáng Jì, Prince of Wǔlíng and Administrator of Kuàijī, was appointed Inspector of Eastern Yángzhōu.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Yuán Shù, Supernumerary Palace Attendant with Scattered Duties, was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of the two prefectures of Northern Qīngzhōu and Yǎnzhōu,
and led his troops on a northern expedition.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Xīnwèi,
righteous volunteers for the northern expedition were granted one rank.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Chéng Jǐngjùn, Inspector of Xúzhōu, captured Wèi Tóngchéng (Wèi Child City).
In the ninth month, on the day Wùshēn,
he again captured Suīlíng Chéng (Suīlíng City).
On the day Wùwǔ,
Zhào Jǐngyuè, Inspector of Northern Yǎnzhōu, besieged Jīngshān.
On the day Rénxū,
Péi Suì, General Who Manifests Awe, raided Shòuyáng,
entered the outer city walls,
but did not succeed.
In Winter, the tenth month, day *Wùyín*
, Péi Suì and Yuán Shù attacked the Wèi city of Jiànlíngchéng,
and captured it.
Day *Xīnsì*
, they further captured Qǔmù.
Commander (General) Sǎolǔ, Péng Bǎosūn, captured Lángyá.
Day *Jiǎshēn*
, they further captured Tánqiūchéng.
Day *Xīnmǎo*
, Péi Suì captured Díchéng.
Day *Bǐngshēn*
, they further captured Pìchéng,
and subsequently advanced to garrison Líjiāng.
Day *Rényín*
, Wèi Administrator (Grand Protector) of Dōnghǎi, Wéi Jìngxīn, surrendered with Sīwúchéng.
General Dìngyuǎn, Administrator (missing two characters) Cáo Shìzōng, captured the Wèi city of Qǔyángchéng.
Day *Jiǎchén*
, they further captured Qínxū.
The Wèi defenders of Méi and Pānxī all abandoned their cities and fled.
In the eleventh month, day *Bǐngchén*
, Péng Bǎosūn captured Dōngguǎnchéng.
Day *Rénxū*
, Péi Suì attacked Ānchéng of Shòuyáng,
and captured it.
Day *Bǐngyín*
, Wèi Mǎtóu and Ānchéng both came and surrendered.
In the twelfth month, day *Wùyín*
, the Wèi city of Jīngshānchéng surrendered.
Day *Yǐsì*
, General Wǔyǒng Lǐ Guóxīng attacked Píngjìngguān,
and captured it.
Day *Xīnchǒu*
, Clerk (Chief Clerk) Xìnwēi Yáng Fǎgān attacked Wǔyángguān;
day *Rényín*
, he attacked Xiànguān: and captured both of them.
The sixth year, Spring, the first month, day *Bǐngwǔ*
, General Ānběi, the Prince of Jìn'ān, Xiāo Gāng, sent his Clerk (Chief Clerk), Liǔ Jīn, to capture Wèi’s Nánxiāng Commandery,
and his Marshal (Sīmǎ), Dǒng Dàngmén, captured Wèi’s Jìnchéng.
Day *Gēngxū*
, they further captured the two cities of Mǎquān and Diāoyáng.
Day *Xīnhài*
, His Majesty personally offered sacrifice in the Southern Suburbs,
and issued a general amnesty upon the land (under Heaven).
Day *Gēngshēn*
, Wèi General Zhèndōng and Inspector (Governor) of Xúzhōu, Yuán Fǎsēng, surrendered with Péngchéng.
Day *Jǐsì*
, the vanguard army of Yōngzhōu captured Wèi’s Xīncài Commandery.
An imperial edict stated:
“The plans of the ancestral temple are established,
and the King’s strategy is now being launched.
The Palace Attendant (Shìzhōng) and General Supervising the Army (Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn), the Marquis of Xīchāng, Xiāo Yuānzǎo,
shall personally command the armies
and lead the vanguard;
General Zhènběi and Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, the Prince of Yùzhāng, Xiāo Zōng, shall manage the fierce heroes,
advancing rapidly like the wind;
the remainder of the armies
shall be dispatched on designated days,
ensuring the initial, middle, and rear forces
are properly and strictly prepared.
We shall then move the Six Armies like clouds,
and cross the river in the Dragon Boat.”
Day *Guǐyǒu*
, Zhèngchéng of Wèi was captured.
Day *Jiǎxū*
, Wèi General Zhèndōng and Inspector of Xúzhōu, Yuán Fǎsēng, was appointed Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
The second month, day *Dīngchǒu*
, the Star of Longevity (*Lǎorén Xīng*) appeared.
Day *Gēngchén*
, Inspector of Nánxúzhōu, the Prince of Lúlíng, Xiāo Xù, returned to court
to receive military instructions.
Day *Yǐwèi*
, Zhào Jǐngyuè took the Wèi city of Lóngkàngchéng.
The third month, day *Bǐngwǔ*
, the Planet Jupiter (*Suìxīng*) appeared in the Southern Dipper (*Nándǒu*).
The leaders of the newly surrendered people were granted exemption from service (or taxes),
and all crimes and faults they had committed were pardoned entirely.
Day *Jǐyǒu*
, the Emperor proceeded to Báixiàchéng,
inspecting the encampments of the Six Armies.
Day *Yǐchǒu*
, General Zhènběi and Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, the Prince of Yùzhāng, Xiāo Zōng, temporarily garrisoned Péngchéng,
taking overall command of all armies,
and concurrently managing the affairs of the Xúzhōu administrative offices.
Day *Jǐsì*
, Wèi Acting General Píngdōng, Yuán Jǐnglóng, was appointed Inspector of Héngzhōu,
and Wèi General Zhēnglǔ, Yuán Jǐngzhòng, was appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
Summer, the fifth month, day *Jǐyǒu*
, the Sùyù Weir was constructed,
and the Cáo Gōng Weir was repaired at Jìyīn.
The Planet Venus (*Tàibái*) was visible during the day.
Day *Rénzǐ*
, Central Protector of the Army (Zhōng Hùjūn) Xiàhóu Dǎn was dispatched to supervise all military affairs at Shòuyáng,
for the Northern Expedition.
The sixth month, day *Gēngchén*
, the Prince of Yùzhāng, Xiāo Zōng, fled to Wèi,
and Wèi reoccupied Péngchéng.
Autumn, the seventh month, day *Rénxū*
, a general amnesty was issued upon the land.
The eighth month, day *Bǐngzǐ*
, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary (Sànqí Chángshì) Cáo Zhòngzōng was concurrently appointed Supervising the Army (Lǐngjūn).
Day *Rénwǔ*
, the Star of Longevity appeared.
The twelfth month, day *Wùzǐ*
, the Prince of Shàolíng, Xiāo Lún, committed a crime;
he was removed from office
and stripped of his rank and domain.
Day *Rénchén*
, there was an earthquake in the capital.
The seventh year, Spring, the first month, day *Xīnchǒu* (the first day of the month)
, crimes punishable by death and lesser offenses were pardoned.
Day *Dīngmǎo*
, the state of Huá sent envoys to present local products.
The second month, day *Jiǎxū*
, the armies of the Northern Expedition ceased strict operations (stood down).
The King of Hénán sent envoys to present local products.
Day *Dīnghài*
, the Star of Longevity appeared.
The third month, day *Yǐmǎo*
, the state of Gāolì (Koguryeo) sent envoys to present local products.
Summer, the fourth month, day *Yǐyǒu*
, Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi), the Prince of Línchuān, Xiāo Hóng, passed away.
The post of Commandant (Xiàowèi) was established at Nánzhōujīn,
and their stipends and ranks were increased.
An edict commanded officials in office
, that each should nominate those they knew,
and all honest officials
should be recommended and brought to attention.
Provinces (Zhōu) should nominate two persons annually,
and large Commanderies (Jùn) one person.
The sixth month, day *Jǐmǎo*
, the state of Línyì (Champa) sent envoys to present local products.
Autumn, the ninth month, day *Jǐyǒu*
, General of Agile Cavalry (Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn), Open Office with the Three Dukes (Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī), and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, the Prince of Póyáng, Xiāo Huī, passed away.
Winter, the tenth month, day *Xīnwèi*
, the Prefect of Dānyáng, the Prince of Xiāngdōng, Xiāo Yì, was appointed Inspector of Jīngzhōu.
The eleventh month, day *Gēngchén*
, a general amnesty was issued upon the land.
On that same day,
Consort Dīng (Dīng Guìpín) passed away.
Day *Xīnsì*
, the armies led by Xiàhóu Dǎn, Hú Lóngyá, Yuán Shù, and Cáo Shìzōng captured Shòuyángchéng.
Day *Dīnghài*
, Wèi Inspector of Yángzhōu, Lǐ Xiàn, was released to return north.
Yùzhōu was established at Shòuyáng,
and Héféi was renamed Nányùzhōu.
Central Protector of the Army, Xiàhóu Dǎn, was appointed Inspector of the two provinces, Yùzhōu and Nányùzhōu.
General Píngxī and Inspector of Yǐngzhōu, Yuán Shù, was promoted to the title of General Ānxī.
Wèi Administrator of Xīnyě surrendered with his commandery.
Dàtōng First Year, Spring, the first month, day *Yǐchǒu*
, Minister of Personnel and Left Assistant (Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè) Xú Miǎn was appointed Minister of Personnel (Shàngshū Púyè)
and General of the Central Guard (Zhōng Wèi Jiāngjūn).
An edict stated:
“We contemplate benefitting the populace,
feeling that the days are insufficient,
and as the seasons cycle,
We constantly promote generosity and simplicity.
The stipends and salaries of the hundred officials
originally had fixed amounts,
but since previous generations,
they have mostly been evaluated and assessed (in kind),
and recently, due to old customs,
there has been no time for reform.
From now on,
they shall be perpetually issued in currency (ready money),
paid out immediately according to schedule,
and must not be delayed or deferred.
Regarding any public property that has been scattered or lost,
regardless of the quantity,
all shall be pardoned.
However, matters involving military provisions
or the collection of public and private property
are not included in this amnesty.”
Day *Xīnwèi*
, His Majesty personally offered sacrifice in the Southern Suburbs.
An edict stated:
“We observe the seasons and perform clear rites,
reverently offering the azure jade,
wishing to inherit the virtue of Heaven
and bestow favor upon the people below.
All those who left their lands due to circumstances
and migrated to other territories
are permitted to return to their homes and livelihoods,
and are granted five years of exemption from labor service.
For the especially poor households,
the ‘Three Contributions’ (*Sāndiào*) shall not be collected.
Those renowned for filial piety, fraternity, and diligence in farming shall be granted one rank of nobility.”
That month
, Inspector of Sīzhōu, Xiàhóu Kuí, advanced his army on the Three Passes (Sānguān),
and captured everywhere he reached.
The third month, day *Xīnwèi*
, His Majesty proceeded to Tóngtài Sì to surrender his body (to the temple).
Day *Jiǎxū*
, he returned to the palace,
issued a general amnesty upon the land,
and changed the era name.
General of the Left Guard (Zuǒ Wèi Jiāngjūn) Xiāo Yuānzǎo was appointed Central Protector of the Army (Zhōng Hùjūn).
Línyì and the Lion Kingdom (Shīzǐguó, Sri Lanka) each sent envoys to present local products.
Summer, the fifth month, day *Bǐngyín*
, Chéng Jǐngjùn captured Wèi’s Líntóng and Zhúyì.
In the eighth month, autumn, on the day Rénchén,
the star of the Elder (Canopus) was seen.
In the tenth month, winter, on the day Gēngxū,
Yuán Qìnghé (元慶和), the Inspector of Dōngyù Zhōu (東豫州) for Wèi (魏), brought Wōyáng (渦陽) to allegiance.
On the day Jiǎyín,
a partial amnesty was granted to Dōngyù Zhōu (東豫州).
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Xiāo Yuānzǎo (蕭淵藻), the Central Protector of the Army, was made Northern Expedition Commander-in-Chief and General Who Conquers the North,
and stationed at Wōyáng (渦陽).
On the day Wùchén,

Yuán Áng (袁昂), Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, Central Guard General, and Minister with the Ceremonial Privilege of Opening a Mansion, was additionally granted the title of Chancellery Supervisor.
Xīxú Zhōu (西徐州) was established at Wōyáng (渦陽).
The state of Gāolí (高麗) sent envoys to offer local products.
In the first month, spring of the second year, on the day Gēngshēn,
Yuán Fǎsēng (元法僧), Minister of Works, was given command of the Central Army General with his current office.

Yuán Áng (袁昂), Chancellery Supervisor, Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, Central Guard General, and Minister with the Ceremonial Privilege of Opening a Mansion, was promoted to the title of General Who Soothes the Central Region.
Xiāo Áng (蕭昂), Minister of the Palace Gate, was made Central Leader of the Army.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the state of Ruìruì (芮芮) sent envoys to offer local products.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the star of the Elder (Canopus) was seen.
In this month,
the Hánshān (寒山) embankment was built.
In the third month, on the day Rénxū,
Jì (績), Prince of Nánkāng (南康) and Inspector of Jiāng Zhōu (江州), was made General Who Pacifies the Right.
In the fourth month, summer, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Yuán Yuàndá (元願達), the Inspector of Yǐng Zhōu (郢州) for Wèi (魏), brought Yìyáng (義陽) to allegiance,
and Běisī Zhōu (北司州) was established.
At this time, Wèi (魏) was in great disorder.
Yuán Hào (元顥), Prince of Běihǎi (北海), Yuán Yù (元彧), Prince of Línhuái (臨淮), and Yuán Yuè (元悅), Prince of Rǔnán (汝南), all came to seek refuge;
Yuán Shìjùn (元世雋), Inspector of Běiqīng Zhōu (北青州), and Lǐ Zhì (李志), Inspector of Nánjīng Zhōu (南荊州), also surrendered with their territories.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīnghài,
Yuán Yù (元彧), Prince of Línhuái (臨淮) of Wèi (魏), requested to return to his home country,
and permission was granted.
In the tenth month, winter, on the day Dīnghài,
Yuán Hào (元顥), Prince of Běihǎi (北海) of Wèi (魏), was made ruler of Wèi (魏),
and Chén Qìngzhī (陳慶之), General of the Palace Guard of the Eastern Palace, was dispatched to escort him back north.
Dèng Xiàn (鄧獻), Inspector of Yù Zhōu (豫州) for Wèi (魏), brought his territory to allegiance.
In the first month of Zhōngdàtōng (中大通) first year, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Southern Suburb,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and those exemplary in filial piety and diligent in agriculture were granted one rank of nobility.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Yuán Yuè (元悅), Prince of Rǔnán (汝南) of Wèi (魏), requested to return to his home country,
and permission was granted.
On the day Xīnsì,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Bright Hall.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Jì (紀), Prince of Wǔlíng (武陵) and Governor of Dānyáng (丹陽), was made Inspector of Jiāng Zhōu (江州).
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the state of Ruìruì (芮芮) sent envoys to offer local products.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Āluózhēn (阿羅真), Prince of Hénán (河南), was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Xīqín (西秦), Hé (河), and Shā (沙) three zhōu.
〔一二〕On the day Gēngchén,
Xiāo Yuānzǎo (蕭淵藻), Central Protector of the Army, was made Central Right General.
In the fourth month, summer, on the day Guǐwèi,
Jì (績), Prince of Nánkāng (南康) and General Who Pacifies the Right, was made Protector General.
On the day Guǐsì,
Chén Qìngzhī (陳慶之) attacked Liángchéng (梁城) of Wèi (魏),
〔一三〕and captured it;
he then advanced and massacred Kǎochéng (考城),
capturing Yuán Huīyè (元暉業), Prince of Jìyīn (濟陰) of Wèi (魏).
In the fifth month, on the day Wùchén,
Dàliáng (大梁) was conquered.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Hǔláo Chéng (虎牢城) was conquered.
Yuán Zǐyōu (元子攸), the ruler of Wèi (魏), abandoned Luòyáng (洛陽),
〔一四〕and fled to Hébĕi (河北).
On the day Yǐhài,
Yuán Hào (元顥) entered Luòyáng (洛陽).
In the sixth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the day Xīnhài,
Jìn Hóng (晉鴻), Administrator of Huáin Yīn (淮陰) for Wèi (魏), brought Húyáng Chéng (湖陽城) to allegiance.
In the intercalary month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Jì (績), Prince of Nánkāng (南康), General Who Pacifies the Right, and Protector General, died.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Ěrzhū Róng (尒朱榮) of Wèi (魏) attacked and killed Yuán Hào (元顥),
and reoccupied Luòyáng (洛陽).
In the ninth month, autumn, on the day Xīnsì,
the ornamental pillars of Zhūquè Háng (朱雀航) suffered a disaster (fire).
Yáng Kǎn (羊侃), General Who Pacifies the North, was made Inspector of Qīng (青) and Jì (冀) two zhōu.
On the day Guǐsì,
the imperial carriage visited Tóngtài Sì (同泰寺),
where a grand assembly (wúzhē dàhuì) for the four communities was held.
Thereupon, the Emperor renounced his body (to become a monk),
and the officials from dukes and ministers downwards
redeemed him with one hundred million coins.
In the tenth month, winter, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace,
a general amnesty was proclaimed,
and the reign era was changed.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Yuán Áng (袁昂), General Who Soothes the Central Region and Minister with the Ceremonial Privilege of Opening a Mansion, was additionally granted the title of Chancellery Supervisor.

Wěi (偉), Prince of Nánpíng (南平), General Who Guards the Garrison and Minister with the Ceremonial Privilege of Opening a Mansion, was additionally granted the title of Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
Xiāo Chēn (蕭琛) and Lù Gǎo (陸杲), Grand Masters of Imperial Lictors with Gold and Purple Seals, were both additionally granted the title of Grand Master of Special Advancement.
Yuán Fǎsēng (元法僧), Minister of Works and Central Army General, was promoted to the title of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
Xiāo Yuānzǎo (蕭淵藻), Central Right General, was made Central Protector General.
〔一五〕Xiāo Áng (蕭昂), Central Leader of the Army, was made Leader of the Army General.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Yán Shǐxīn (嚴始欣), Inspector of Bā Zhōu (巴州) for Wèi (魏), surrendered with his city.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngsì,
the state of Pánpán (盤盤) sent envoys to offer local products.
In the first month, spring of the second year, on the day Wùyín,
Gāng (綱), Prince of Jìn'ān (晉安) and Inspector of Yōng Zhōu (雍州), was made General-in-Chief of Cavalry and Inspector of Yáng Zhōu (揚州).
Xù (續), Prince of Lúlíng (廬陵) and Inspector of Nánxú Zhōu (南徐州), was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yōng Zhōu (雍州).
On the day Guǐwèi,
the star of the Elder (Canopus) was seen.
In the fourth month, summer, on the day Gēngshēn,
there was a heavy hailstorm.
On the day Rénshēn,
Fófǔ (佛輔), Prince of Hénán (河南), was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Xīqín (西秦) and Hé (河) two zhōu.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Yuán Yuè (元悅), Grand Tutor of Wèi (魏) and Prince of Rǔnán (汝南), was sent back north to be the ruler of Wèi (魏).
On the day Gēngshēn,
Fàn Zūn (范遵), Left Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat for Wèi (魏), was made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Sī Zhōu (司州),
to accompany Yuán Yuè (元悅) on his northern expedition.
The state of Línyì (林邑) sent envoys to offer local products.
On the day Rénshēn,
the state of Fúnán (扶南) sent envoys to offer local products.
In the eighth month, autumn, on the day Gēngxū,
the imperial carriage visited Déyáng Táng (德陽堂),
where a music performance (sīzhú huì) was held,
to bid farewell to Yuán Yuè (元悅), the ruler of Wèi (魏).
Mountain bandits gathered,
and raided the counties under Kuàijī Jùn (會稽郡).
In the ninth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Zhàn Hǎizhēn (湛海珍), Acting General of Transcendent Valour, was granted an imperial staff to suppress them.
〔一六〕
In the first month, spring of the third year, on the day Xīnsì,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Southern Suburb,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and those exemplary in filial piety and diligent in agriculture were granted one rank of nobility.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Zhèng Xiānhù (鄭先護), Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat for Wèi (魏), was made General Who Conquers the North.
In the second month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Bright Hall.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the star of the Elder (Canopus) was seen.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Xiāo Chēn (蕭琛), Grand Master of Special Advancement, died.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Yuán Jǐnglóng (元景隆), Inspector of Guǎng Zhōu (廣州), was made General Who Pacifies the Right.
In the fourth month, summer, on the day Yǐsì,
Huáng Tàizǐ Tǒng (皇太子統) died.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Xiāo Yuānyóu (蕭淵猷), former Palace Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, was made Central Protector of the Army.
Xú Miǎn (徐勉), Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat, was additionally granted the titles of Grand Master of Special Advancement and Grand Master of Imperial Lictors of the Right.
The state of Dāndān (丹丹) sent envoys to offer local products.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Huān (歡), Duke of Huáróng (華容) and Inspector of Nánxú Zhōu (南徐州), son of Zhāomíng Tàizǐ (昭明太子), was established as Prince of Yùzhāng Jùn (豫章郡);
Yù (譽), Duke of Zhījiāng (枝江), was established as Prince of Hédōng Jùn (河東郡);
Chá (詧), Duke of Qū'ā (曲阿), was established as Prince of Yuèyáng Jùn (岳陽郡).
In the seventh month, autumn, on the day Yǐhài,
Gāng (綱), Prince of Jìn'ān (晉安), was established as the Crown Prince.
A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and those who succeeded their fathers, and those who were loyal and filial, civil and military, clean and diligent in their positions,
were all granted one rank of nobility.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Xiè Jǔ (謝舉), Imperial Attendant and Minister of the Five Military Bureaus, was made Minister of Personnel.
On the day Gēngyín,
an imperial edict stated:
“Extending favour to the six kindred,
and glorifying the nine generations,
granting them marquisates,
is also deemed just.
All imperial relatives with close ties
may be granted the title of Marquis of a Hamlet (xiāngtíng hóu) with a stipend,
with ranks varying according to their proximity.
As for those who are close relatives,
they shall follow the old regulations.”
On the day Rénchén,
Hé Jìngrōng (何敬容), Minister of Personnel, was made Right Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat.
On the day Guǐsì,
the star of the Elder (Canopus) was seen.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Xiāo Yuānzǎo (蕭淵zǎo), Palace Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, was made General Who Conquers the North and Inspector of Nányǎn Zhōu (南兗州).
On the day Wùyín,
the state of Lángyáxiū (狼牙脩) submitted a memorial and offered local products.
In the tenth month, winter, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the imperial entourage visited Tóngtài Sì (同泰寺).
Gāozǔ (高祖) ascended the Dharma seat
to expound the meaning of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra and Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra to the four communities,
〔一七〕until the day Yǐmǎo.
Xiāo Zhèngzé (蕭正則), former Marquis of Lèshān Xiàn (樂山縣), was guilty and banished.
At this time, he enticed fugitives
to raid Guǎng Zhōu (廣州),
but was suppressed by local forces.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the imperial entourage visited Tóngtài Sì (同泰寺).
Gāozǔ (高zǔ) ascended the Dharma seat
to expound the meaning of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra to the four communities,
ending on the day Xīnchǒu of the twelfth month.
In this year,
wild grain grew in Wúxīng Jùn (吳興郡),
which was fit for consumption.
In the spring, the first month, *bǐngyín* *shuò*, of the fourth year
, Wěi, the Prince of Nánpíng, who was the General-in-chief Who Guards the Commandery and *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*, was promoted to the position of *Dà Sīmǎ* (Grand Marshal).
Yuán Fǎsēng, the *Sīkōng* (Minister of Works), was promoted to the position of *Tàiwèi* (Grand Commandant)
. Yuán Áng, who was the Prefect of the Department of State Affairs, the General-in-chief of the Central Army, and *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*, was promoted to the position of *Sīkōng*
. Zhèngdé, the son of Hóng, the Prince Jìnghuì of Línchuān, was established as the Commandery Prince of Línhè
. On *wùchén*
, Lún, the Prince of Shàolíng, who was the Governor of Dānyáng, was made the Inspector of Yángzhōu
. Xuē Fǎhù, the Commander of the Crown Prince's Right Guard, was made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Sīzhōu
, and escorted Yuán Yuè to Luò
. On *gēngwǔ*
, Dàqì, the principal imperial grandson, was established as the Commandery Prince of Xuānchéng
. On *guǐwèi*
, Liú Shìmíng, the Inspector of Wèi's Nányǎnzhōu, surrendered his city
. Wèi's Nányǎnzhōu was changed to Qiáozhōu
, and Shìmíng was made its Inspector
. In the second month, on *rén'yín*
, the Elder Star (*Lǎorén Xīng*) appeared
. Yuán Fǎsēng, the newly appointed *Tàiwèi*, returned to the North
and became ruler of the Eastern Wèi
. Yuán Jǐnglóng, the General Who Pacifies the Right, was made General Who Campaigns in the North and Inspector of Xúzhōu
; Yáng Kǎn, the General of Cloud Banners, was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yǎnzhōu
; and Yuán Shù, the Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, was made General Who Guards the North
. On *gēngxū*
, Lún, the Prince of Shàolíng, the newly appointed Inspector of Yángzhōu, committed a crime
and was dismissed, becoming a commoner
. On *rénzǐ*
, Jì, the Prince of Wǔlíng, who was the Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, was made the Inspector of Yángzhōu
; and Xiāo Áng, the General Who Commands the Army, was made the Inspector of Jiāngzhōu
. On *bǐngchén*
, one white deer was captured in Shàolíng County
. In the third month, on *gēngwǔ*

, Xiāo Zǐxiǎn, the Palace Attendant and concurrent Academian of the Directorate of Education, presented a memorial proposing the establishment of one Assistant Instructor for the *Xiàojīng* (Classic of Filial Piety) based on the imperial decree
, and ten students
, dedicated solely to mastering the meaning of the *Xiàojīng* as interpreted by Gāozǔ
. In summer, the fourth month, on *rénshēn*
, the kingdom of Pánpán dispatched an envoy to present local products
. In autumn, the seventh month, on *jiǎchén*
, stars fell like rain
. In the eighth month, on *bǐngzǐ*
, Lù Gǎo, the Attendant with Special Advancement, died
. In the ninth month, on *yǐsì*
, Kè, the Heir Apparent of the Prince of Nánpíng, who was the Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, was made General Who Commands the Army
; Xù, the Prince of Lúlíng, who was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yōngzhōu, was made General Who Pacifies the North
; Yì, the Prince of Xiāngdōng, who was Commander of the Western Gentlemen and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was made General Who Pacifies the West
; and Yuán Áng, the *Sīkōng*, concurrently took the title of Prefect of the Department of State Affairs
In the eleventh month, on *jǐyǒu*
, the kingdom of Gāolì dispatched an envoy to present local products
. In the twelfth month, on *gēngchén*
, Yuán Fǎsēng, the *Tàiwèi*, was made General-in-chief of Cavalry, accorded the ceremony of *Kāifǔ Tóng Sānsī*, and Inspector of Yǐngzhōu
. In the spring, the first month, on *xīnmǎo*, of the fifth year
, the imperial chariot personally offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburb
, granting a general amnesty across the realm
. Those distinguished by filial piety, fraternal duty, and diligent farming were granted one grade of nobility
. The day before, during the night of *bǐng*
, Xiè Dízhī, the Prefect of the Southern Suburb, and others went to the site to carry out the preparations
. They suddenly heard three instances of strange fragrance in the air carried by the wind
. When the ceremony was about to commence
, and after the music for welcoming the spirits concluded
, a divine light filled the altar
, multicolored in vermilion, purple, yellow, and white
. It disappeared only after the duration of a meal
. Jì, the Prince of Wǔlíng, concurrently the Grand Tutor, and others reported this
. On *wùshēn*
, the capital experienced an earthquake
. On *jǐyǒu*
, a long star appeared
. On *xīnhài*
, the imperial chariot personally offered sacrifice at the Bright Hall (*Míngtáng*)
. On *guǐchǒu*
, Dàqì, the Prince of Xuānchéng, was made General of the Central Army
. The kingdom of Hénán dispatched an envoy to present local products
. In the second month, on *guǐwèi*
, the Emperor proceeded to Tóngtài Temple
and held the Grand Assembly of the Four Divisions
. Gāozǔ ascended the Dharma seat
and recited the topic headings of the *Móhē Bōrě Jīng* (Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra) inscribed in gold characters
. This concluded on *jǐchǒu*
. The Elder Star appeared
. In the third month, on *bǐngchén*
, Wěi, the Prince of Nánpíng, the *Dà Sīmǎ*, died
. In summer, the fourth month, on *guǐyǒu*
, Zāng Dùn, the Imperial Censor, was concurrently made General Who Commands the Army
. In the fifth month, on *wùzǐ*
, the capital experienced a great flood
, and boats could navigate the Imperial Way
. In the sixth month, on *jǐmǎo*
, Lán Bǎo, the lord of Wèi's Jiànyì city, killed the Inspector of Wèi's Dōngxúzhōu
, and surrendered with Xiàpī city
. In autumn, the seventh month, on *xīnmǎo*
, Xiàpī was changed to Wǔzhōu
. In the eighth month, on *gēngshēn*
, Yuán Jǐnglóng, the former Inspector of Xúzhōu, was made General Who Pacifies the Right
. The Elder Star appeared
. On *jiǎzǐ*
, the kingdom of Bōsī dispatched an envoy to present local products
. On *jiǎshēn*
, Xiāo Yuānyóu, the Commandant of the Central Guard, died
. In the ninth month, on *jǐhài*
, Zhèngdé, the Prince of Línhè and General of Light Chariots, was made Commandant of the Central Guard
. On *jiǎyín*
, Yuán Áng, the Prefect of the Department of State Affairs and *Sīkōng*, was made Attendant with Special Advancement and Grand Master of the Left Glorious Happiness
, retaining his position as *Sīkōng*
. The kingdom of Pánpán dispatched an envoy to present local products
. In winter, the tenth month, on *gēngshēn*
, Hé Jìngrōng, the Right Assistant Prefect of the Department of State Affairs, was made Left Assistant Prefect of the Department of State Affairs
; Xiè Jǔ, the President of the Board of Civil Office, was made Right Assistant Prefect of the Department of State Affairs
; and Xiāo Zǐxiǎn, the Palace Attendant and Libationer of the Directorate of Education, was made President of the Board of Civil Office
. In the spring, the second month, on *guǐhài*, of the sixth year
, the imperial chariot personally ploughed the ceremonial field (*Jìtián*)
, granting a general amnesty across the realm
. Those distinguished by filial piety, fraternal duty, and diligent farming were granted one grade of nobility
. In the third month, on *jǐhài*
, Kětà Zhèn, the acting Prince of Hénán, was made Inspector of Xīqín and Hézhōu, and Prince of Hénán
. On *jiǎchén*
, the kingdom of Bǎijì dispatched an envoy to present local products
. In summer, the fourth month, on *dīngmǎo*
, Yínghuò (Mars) was in Nándǒu (Southern Dipper constellation)
. In autumn, the seventh month, on *jiǎchén*
, the kingdom of Línyì dispatched an envoy to present local products
. In the eighth month, on *jǐwèi*
, Yáng Shàoxiān, the Prince of Wǔxīng and Inspector of Nánliángzhōu, was made Inspector of Qínzhōu and Nánqínzhōu
. In winter, the tenth month, on *dīngmǎo*
, Yuán Qìnghé, the General of Trustworthy Valour, was made General Who Guards the North
, and led the troops on a northern campaign
. In the intercalary twelfth month, on *bǐngwǔ*
, there were two thunderclaps in the southwest
. In the spring, the first month, *wùshēn* *shuò*, of the first year of *Dàtóng*
, the reign title was changed
, and a general amnesty was granted across the realm
In the second month, on *jǐmǎo*
, the Elder Star appeared
. On *xīnsì*
, the imperial chariot personally offered sacrifice at the Bright Hall
. On *dīnghài*
, the imperial chariot personally ploughed the ceremonial field
. On *xīnchǒu*
, the kingdom of Gāolì and the kingdom of Dāndān each dispatched envoys to present local products
. In the third month, on *xīnwèi*
, Ānlèsàdānwáng, the King of Huá Guó, dispatched an envoy to present local products
. In summer, the fourth month, on *gēngzǐ*
, the kingdom of Bōsī presented local products
. On *jiǎchén*
, Liú Jì, Wèi's General Who Guards the East, was made Inspector of Xúzhōu
. On *rénxū*
, Xù, the Prince of Lúlíng and General Who Pacifies the North, was made General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu
. In autumn, the seventh month, on *yǐmǎo*
, the Elder Star appeared
. On *xīnmǎo*
, the kingdom of Fúnán dispatched an envoy to present local products
. In winter, the tenth month, on *xīnmǎo*
, Xiāo Yuānzǎo, the former Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, was made General Protector of the Army
. In the eleventh month, on *dīngwèi*
, Xú Miǎn, the General Who Guards the Center, Attendant with Special Advancement, and Grand Master of the Right Glorious Happiness, died
. On *rénxū*
, Lán Qīn, the Inspector of Běiliángzhōu, attacked Hànzhōng
and conquered it
. Yuán Luó, Wèi's Inspector of Liángzhōu, surrendered
. On *guǐhài*
, those from Liángzhōu who had submitted were granted graded tax exemptions and labor service remissions
. On *jiǎzǐ*
, Yáng Fǎshēn, the Prince of Yīnpíng, who was the General of Heroic Valour and Inspector of Běiyìzhōu, was promoted to the title of General Who Pacifies the North
. The moon passed by the star Zuǒjiǎo
. In the twelfth month, on *yǐyǒu*
, Yáng Huīyì, Wèi's Inspector of Běixúzhōu, was made General Who Pacifies the North
. On *wùxū*
, Yáng Shàoxiān, the Prince of Wǔxīng, who was General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qínzhōu and Nánqínzhōu, was promoted to the title of General of Chariots and Cavalry
; and Yáng Fǎshēn, the Prince of Yīnpíng, who was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Běiyìzhōu, was promoted to the title of General-in-chief of Cavalry
. On *xīnchǒu*
, Yì, the Prince of Xiāngdōng, who was General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was promoted to the title of General Who Guards the West
. In the spring, the first month, on *jiǎchén*, of the second year
, Zāng Dùn, the concurrent General Who Commands the Army, was made General Who Commands the Central Army
In the second month, on *yǐhài*
, the imperial chariot personally ploughed the ceremonial field
. On *bǐngxū*
, the Elder Star appeared.
In the third month, on the day Gēngshēn,
an edict stated:
"Governance lies in nourishing the people,
virtue exists in covering all beings.
The commands from above are like the wind;
the people respond like grass.
I, relying on meager virtue,
found fate arrived with the proper time,
bringing order out of chaos and returning to correctness.
This has lasted for three *jǐ* (36 years).
Yet I have been unable to ensure that heavy gates remain unlocked,
or that defenses are maintained overseas.
Borders and territories are filled with obstacles,
and carriages and writings (standards) are not yet unified.
The people are exhausted by transportation levies,
and the soldiers are weary from border defense.
Fields have been cleared for provisions,
and the situation has not been able to achieve stable respite.
The principles of governing are unclear,
and policies are often biased.
Among the many officials, there are no words offered from sincere hearts,
and the four faculties of hearing lack the ability to listen rapidly (to distant voices).
The provinces neglect investigative inspection (*cì jǔ*),
and the commanderies forget shared governance.
This leads to injustices and the bearing of slander,
with no means for these voices to be heard,
and those who insult statutes and play with laws
use these situations to create wickedness.
The Petition Stone (*Fèishí*) is displayed in vain,
and the suspended bell (*Xuánzhōng*) is set up to no effect.
Does not the *Shū* (Book of Documents) say: 'Ministers are the limbs and bones,
and good officials are the sages.'?
I truly rely on worthy assistants
to correct my deficiencies.
All who are in court
should each present upright advice.
Matters of governance that are inconvenient for the people
may all be submitted.
If you are in the four distant regions,
Inspectors (*cìshǐ*), officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank (*èrqiānshí*), and chief administrators
should all report them through memorials.
If ordinary people have matters to speak of,
let them all be conveyed.
I shall personally examine them
to relieve these faults.
Civil and military officials in their positions,
nominate those whom you know.
Dukes, Marquises, generals, and ministers
shall be promoted and employed according to their talent.
Gather the omitted and mend the defects;
do not hide anything."
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Yǐwèi,

Yuán Fǎsēng, who held the status of Pīnjì Dàjiāngjūn (General of Agile Cavalry) and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī (Establishing a Government Office and Possessing the Same Authority as the Three Ducal Ministers), was made Tàiwèi (Grand Commandant),
leading the Jūnshī Jiāngjūn (General of the Army Mentor).
Prior to this,
Jiāng Zisì, Shàngshū Yòuchéng (Assistant Director of the Right in the Department of State Affairs), submitted a sealed memorial,
speaking strongly about the successes and failures of governance.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
an edict stated:
"The ancients had a saying,
'When the roof leaks, the fault is above,
but knowledge of it is below.'
The faults that I have accumulated
I cannot realize myself.
Concerning the sealed memorials of Jiāng Zisì and others, as previously submitted,
the Department of State Affairs (*Shàngshū*) should frequently review and investigate them.
If anything causes harm or suffering to the people,
it should be immediately halted and suspended.
You should promptly and thoroughly report (your findings),
without allowing for delay or sluggishness."
On the day Yǐsì,
Yuán Luó, formerly the Cìshǐ of Liángzhōu under the Wèi, was made Zhēng Běi Dàjiāngjūn (General-in-Chief Who Conquers the North) and Cìshǐ of the two provinces of Qīngzhōu and Jìzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīnghài,
an edict stated:
"The functionaries (*lìng*) of the Southern Suburb (*Nánjiāo*), the Hall of Light (*Míngtáng*), the Imperial Mausoleums and Temples (*Língmiào*), and others
have the same rank as those performing Court Attendance (*Cháoqǐng*),
which is too light for their duties.
This may be changed to equal the rank of Sǎnqí Shìláng (Gentleman-in-Attendance with Wide Counsel)."
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Yǐhài,
an edict ordered a massive northern campaign.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐhài,
an edict ordered the northern expeditionary forces to withdraw.
On the day Xīnhài,
the capital suffered an earthquake.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénshēn,
the Wèi requested establishing peaceful relations,
and an edict granted permission.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Zhāng Zuǎn, the Prefect of Wúxīng, Fùmǎ Dūwèi (General Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law), and Marquis of Lìtíng, was made Lìbù Shàngshū (Minister of the Ministry of Personnel).
In the third year, spring, the first month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the Imperial Carriage personally performed sacrifice in the Southern Suburb (*Nánjiāo*),
and a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm;
those distinguished by filial piety, fraternal duty, and diligence in agriculture were bestowed one rank of nobility.
That night,
the Zhūquè Gate suffered a fire.
On the day Rén Yín,
the sky was cloudless,
yet ash fell like rain,
yellowish in color.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Shào Líng Wáng Lún, the Zhōngshū Lìng (Director of the Central Secretariat), was made Cìshǐ of Jiāngzhōu.
In the second month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
the Star of the Old Man (*Lǎorén Xīng*) appeared.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Imperial Carriage personally plowed the Ceremonial Field (*Jìtián*).
